tiles.summary: The human-worn counterpart to Voller AI Skins: a concept for customisable suits combining personal character design, wearer-controlled interaction and AI assistance. It carries forward the proposed bearing-shell, ribbon and shared AI Fisherman ideas, adapted to a human wearer. These mechanisms and any physical benefits remain unvalidated. The hand controllers and suit are intended to work together as one system: wearer commands would pass through the controllers to the suit, with AI feedback in the same interaction design. This connection is a design requirement and has not yet been demonstrated in hardware. The proposed first step is a digital suit mock-up showing controller inputs, gestures and simulated suit/AI feedback together. Human-use hardware would require separate engineering and safety testing; no working suit, flight, protective performance or delivery date is being offered. Explore three proposed configurations: a suit with linked hand controllers; fairy wings as a separate wearable module; or the suit and wings together. The wings are optional. Each physical configuration still needs its own engineering and testing. In the Copper Tunnel concept, the suit is intended to provide a protective outer layer, while wings remain an optional separate wearable. No impact, abrasion, collision or other protective rating has been established. See the Paris flight concept artwork at https://voller-ai-skins.good-badge-3270.chatgpt.site/portfolio.html#paris-flight.

tiles.summary: A proposed AI fairy-wing wearable with translucent, iridescent panels, fine silver bearing details and a choice of gold or cyan accents. Explore it as a separate wearable module or as an optional addition to Super Super Suits; wearing both is not a requirement of the concept. A standalone version would need its own suitable attachment and control design. Suit compatibility, lift, flight and human-use safety remain unvalidated. The current artwork shows the combined configuration; it is not a working-product demonstration. The proposed wing modes include precise following of lazy-river routes, gliding, twirling, ribbon combinations and rhythm-led movement. These describe the intended experience, not measured flight performance. See the Paris flight concept artwork at https://voller-ai-skins.good-badge-3270.chatgpt.site/portfolio.html#paris-flight.
